reason: Prior outcomes give no promoted alternative: the K-loop edits failed eligibility or lost, and the supplied historical scores cannot establish a benefit. For this role, transpose_fusion ranks first because it directly tests fewer A scratch writes and reads while requiring explicit accounting for ZA transfers and repacking. a_transpose tests a simpler compact A panel, but changes panel lifetime and consumer strides. B-panel packing proposals rank next: B is already read contiguously, so their added timed packing cost has uncertain upside. Cache and store/schedule proposals have less direct evidence of reducing A conversion cost; the direct ZA store also lacks supplied evidence of a legal encoding. All are unverified hypotheses, and correctness risk rises for proposals that change scratch lifetime, stride, or store mapping.
